items.headline: Greed rebounds to 75 while Valuation rises to 87; PRICE_DISCIPLINE remains active
items.summary: The AGCI live engine reads Greed 75/100, up 12 points day over day but still 6 points lower over seven days, while Valuation rises to 87/100. The regime remains Correction and the matrix condition stays PRICE_DISCIPLINE — Wait / Price discipline.
items.whyItMatters: Friday's rebound restored risk appetite quickly without repairing aggregate valuation. The combination argues against interpreting one strong session as a new broad-risk entry point.

items.newsletter: Saudi East-West pipeline / Barron's Daily Roundup / 11-12 Sep 2026
items.headline: Saudi Arabia shuts East-West oil pipeline after drone attack, weakening a key Hormuz bypass
items.summary: Saudi Arabia temporarily shut its East-West pipeline after a drone attack damaged the route. The pipeline can move roughly 4–5 million barrels per day and is a critical export alternative while Hormuz is impaired. The same regional shock is now intersecting with Houthi advances near Bab el-Mandeb.
items.whyItMatters: The energy shock is no longer concentrated in one maritime chokepoint. Damage to a major bypass route raises the tail risk for crude, diesel, freight, insurance and inflation even if spot oil temporarily retraces.
items.agciSignal: MULTI-CHOKEPOINT ENERGY RISK / HEDGE MODERATE / DO NOT CHASE

items.newsletter: U.S. markets / Review & Preview: Time to Hike / 11-12 Sep 2026
items.headline: Markets price a high probability of a September Fed hike as 10-year yield approaches 5%
items.summary: After firm August CPI, markets moved to roughly an 85% probability of a 25 bp Fed increase at the September 15–16 meeting. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached about 4.99%. Stocks still rallied more than 1% on Friday, underscoring that short-term risk appetite and discount-rate pressure are moving in opposite directions.
items.whyItMatters: A near-5% 10-year yield materially raises the hurdle rate for long-duration equities, real estate and leveraged strategies. The equity rebound should therefore be judged against cash-flow durability and valuation rather than momentum alone.
items.agciSignal: FED HIKE RISK HIGH / 10Y NEAR 5% / DURATION DISCIPLINE

items.headline: Nvidia discusses anchor investment in Anthropic IPO as AI capital loops deepen
items.summary: Nvidia is in talks to become an anchor investor in Anthropic's planned IPO, potentially committing up to USD 10 billion, according to Reuters sources. The proposed transaction would deepen financial ties between a leading GPU supplier and one of its largest AI-compute customers.
items.whyItMatters: The deal would reinforce AI demand but also heighten the need to separate independently funded end demand from strategic supplier-customer capital loops. AGCI should continue testing counterparties, financing structure, utilization, margins and free cash flow.
items.agciSignal: AI CAPITAL LOOP / DEMAND QUALITY TEST / COUNTERPARTY DISCIPLINE

items.headline: QatarEnergy seeks multi-year U.S. LNG supply as Gulf damage shifts from temporary disruption to structural sourcing
items.summary: QatarEnergy is seeking multi-year LNG supply contracts from U.S. producers through 2031 after damage to Ras Laffan facilities sidelined about 12.8 million tonnes per year of capacity. The move shifts part of the response from spot-market substitution toward longer-duration procurement.
items.whyItMatters: Long-term replacement contracting is evidence that some Gulf energy disruptions may persist well beyond a short tactical shock. It improves strategic optionality for U.S. LNG exporters while increasing the importance of capacity, shipping and contract quality.
items.agciSignal: LNG RECONTRACTING / U.S. EXPORT OPTIONALITY / LONGER-DURATION GULF DISRUPTION

items.headline: Trump says Chinese automakers could build in the U.S. but opposes using Mexico as an export platform
items.category: Mexico / USMCA / Autos / China / Industrial Real Estate
items.summary: President Trump said he would be open to Chinese automakers manufacturing in the United States with American workers, while opposing Chinese vehicles built in Mexico and imported into the U.S. Existing U.S. restrictions and political opposition remain substantial.
items.whyItMatters: For Mexico, the signal reinforces that Chinese-linked automotive investment faces a higher policy hurdle even if broader U.S.–Mexico trade negotiations advance. Nearshoring remains attractive, but origin of capital and end-market rules matter more than headline capacity.
items.agciSignal: MEXICO CHINA-SCREENING RISK / AUTO CONTENT DISCIPLINE / SELECTIVE NEARSHORING
